title: AI Shelf Space Readiness Score
subtitle: Measures how well your consumer brand is positioned to win the AI shortlist — the new discovery layer in ChatGPT, Gemini, and Amazon Rufus.

questions.text: How consistently does your brand appear by name in ChatGPT, Gemini, or Amazon Rufus for your core category queries?

answers.label: We have never checked
We checked once or twice and took a screenshot — we assumed it was stable
We run occasional checks but have no systematic process
We run regular checks across multiple query types and log the results
We run high-volume continuous monitoring across marketplaces and platforms — we know our brand rotation rate

questions.text: Amazon Rufus names an average of 2.2 brands per answer. How often is your brand one of them for your category's buying queries?

answers.label: No idea — we have not looked
We have seen our brand appear a few times but cannot say how consistently
We appear sometimes, but other brands dominate — we do not know why
We appear regularly and we have started to understand which queries drive that
We appear consistently across our priority queries and actively manage our shortlist position

questions.text: In 34% of Rufus responses, a brand is named in the text but has no matching product card in the carousel. How confident are you that your brand name and listings are properly aligned in AI responses?

answers.label: We have not looked — this is the first time we have heard of this mismatch
We assume they are aligned because our listings look fine
We have checked a handful of queries and spotted some mismatches
We have audited alignment and fixed the obvious gaps
We monitor brand-to-carousel alignment regularly across our catalog

low.headline: You are not on the shortlist — and you do not know it
low.text: Rufus names about two brands per answer. If you checked visibility once and assumed it was stable, you are missing most of the picture. In 70,000 queries we ran, only 13% of categories had one brand lead consistently — the rest rotated. An average of 3.7 different brands took the first-named slot. A screenshot is not a strategy.
steps: Run your top 20 category queries through ChatGPT, Gemini and Amazon Rufus this week — not once, across multiple days on a clean account with no purchase history
Check whether your brand appears in both the Rufus text response AND the product card carousel — they are often misaligned and that gap costs you sales
Treat AI search as a separate monitoring job from SEO — the inputs, query shapes and brand signals are different

mid.headline: You are on the map but not consistently on the shortlist
mid.text: You know your brand appears sometimes. The challenge is that visibility fluctuates — 3.7 different brands rotate through the first-named slot on average. Knowing you appeared yesterday tells you nothing about today. You need consistent data, not snapshots.
steps: Move from occasional checks to running the same queries repeatedly across clean accounts — consistency in the inputs is how you spot real shifts
Map which query types surface your brand versus which surface competitors — the gap tells you where to improve content and product signals
Fix any text-to-carousel mismatches immediately — they mean Rufus is recommending you but shoppers cannot find your product

high.headline: You are tracking the shortlist — now turn data into strategy
high.text: Systematic monitoring puts you ahead of most consumer brands. The next move is feeding that visibility data into your ad targeting and content decisions so AI visibility translates into sales, not just impressions.
steps: Wire AI visibility data into your ad strategy — the queries where you appear consistently should inform your keyword targeting on Amazon and Google
Build a shortlist-to-sale attribution model that connects AI recommendations to downstream branded search volume and conversion
Track lead-brand rotation in your category over time — shifts in who holds the slot are commercial signals worth acting on

questions.text: Rufus filters on sales velocity, reviews, and ratings before it reads a single word of your content. How well does your core Amazon range meet that eligibility bar?

answers.label: Most of our products have under 50 reviews or sit below 4 stars — we are probably being filtered out before content is read
A few hero SKUs qualify but the rest of our range does not
Around half our range meets the threshold for Rufus consideration
Most of our range qualifies and we have a process to push new SKUs through the eligibility bar
Our full range meets the eligibility threshold and we track this as a primary operational metric

questions.text: Once a product is eligible, content is what gets it recommended. How has your product content been written?

answers.label: Written for old-school keyword search — short fragments and dense terms, not how a human asks a question
Human-readable copy but not structured for how AI reads, retrieves and cites product content
We have started rewriting some listings with AI recommendation in mind
We have a content approach built around AI retrieval — question-answering, use-case led, ingredient and benefit structured
All live content is engineered for AI readability and we update it based on what query data shows AI is asking for

questions.text: How many active SKUs does your brand currently have listed on Amazon?
questions.hint: Count individual variants — size, flavour, colour — as separate SKUs

questions.text: How many of those SKUs have 50 or more reviews AND a rating of 4.0 stars or above?
questions.hint: These are roughly the thresholds Rufus applies before reading any content — below them, your copy does not matter

low.headline: Rufus is filtering you out before it reads a word
low.text: The most important finding from the Publicis Groupe Rufus data: eligibility gates fire before content. A weak product cannot be written into the shortlist. If your SKUs are below the review and rating threshold, the best content in the world gets you nowhere. Fix the product fundamentals first.
steps: Identify your top five revenue SKUs and make getting them above the review and rating bar the priority — not a nice-to-have
Set up a post-purchase review request sequence if you do not have one — review velocity matters as much as total review count
Hold off on content rewrites for ineligible products — eligibility first, then content engineering

mid.headline: Some of your range is in the game — your content probably is not
mid.text: You have eligible products. The challenge is that content written for keyword-match search does not work for conversational AI retrieval. Rufus reads to answer a shopper question. Your content needs to do the same thing.
steps: Pull your most conversational Google Search Console queries for your category — they are the closest proxy for what Rufus is asking about your products
Rewrite A+ content and bullet points to answer use-case questions rather than stack keyword fragments
Build a pipeline to push new product launches through the eligibility threshold before you spend time on content

high.headline: You are eligible and your content is working for you
high.text: You have cleared the eligibility bar and built content AI can read and retrieve. The next step is making sure the broader signal environment confirms what your listings claim — third-party reviews, community conversations, independent coverage AI can find outside your own pages.
steps: Audit where AI systems can find proof of your brand claims outside your own site and Amazon listing
Seed independent review platforms and category subreddits with genuine content from real customers
Feed AI visibility data back into your content update cycle — if a query type is not surfacing your brand, the content gap is usually findable

questions.text: The eCommerce journey is shifting from Search → PDP → Checkout → Payment to Intent → AI Agent → Product Selection → Permission → Payment. Where is your brand's thinking on this?

answers.label: We are focused on the current channel journey — this feels like a future problem
We know it is coming but have not changed how we work
We have started thinking about what it means for our discovery and content strategy
We have made concrete changes to content and presence to position for agent-driven discovery
Agentic commerce is central to our growth strategy and we are building for it now

questions.text: Consumers are starting to build personal buying agents that watch markets and purchase when conditions are met. How machine-readable and discoverable is your brand to an AI agent evaluating your category?

answers.label: We have no idea what a buying agent would see when it looks at our category
We assume our current listings are sufficient — we have not looked at this specifically
We have audited our product data quality but have not optimised for agent retrieval
We have clean, structured product data and a strategy for being on the agent's shortlist
We have tested our brand from an agent's point of view — we know what it finds and have optimised for it

questions.text: Mastercard is building Agent Pay — infrastructure for AI agents to make purchases on behalf of consumers. Discovery, selection and payment are all becoming agentic. How are you planning accordingly?

answers.label: We have not thought about what happens when AI handles the full purchase journey
We are aware of the direction but it feels early to act
We are starting to plan for agent-compatible discovery and structured product data
We have a roadmap that treats AI agents as a buyer cohort, not a channel feature
Agentic buying infrastructure is already part of our product and commercial strategy

low.headline: You are optimising for a journey that is already changing underneath you
low.text: Mastercard is talking about it on earnings calls. Amazon Rufus is live. Consumers are building personal buying agents for high-ticket items. The brands that win the next five years are the ones treating AI agents as their next buyer cohort, not a future curiosity. The window to build ahead of mainstream adoption is now.
steps: Map your current customer journey and identify at which step an AI agent could replace or shortcut it — the answer tells you where to prioritise
Audit your product data for machine readability — missing specs and inconsistent fields are invisible to humans but fatal for agent evaluation
Think about your brand as a set of signals an agent reads: run your category in ChatGPT Shopping and see whether your product makes the list

mid.headline: You see the shift — now build infrastructure ahead of it
mid.text: You understand agentic commerce is real. The gap is converting awareness into infrastructure. Brands that win this space will not be the ones who reacted fastest — they will be the ones who had repeatable systems in place before everyone else noticed.
steps: Prioritise structured product data and schema as a foundation — it serves both AI search and agent-driven selection at the same time
Build a consistent signal environment across every surface an AI agent might check: your site, Amazon, Reddit, independent review platforms
Start tracking which content types drive AI citation — then build systems around what works

high.headline: You are building for the right future
high.text: Most consumer brands are still fighting for Google page one. You are building for the layer above it. The next 12 months will see a lot more brands wake up to agentic commerce — your advantage is the infrastructure, content and data head start.
steps: Test your brand from inside an actual agent workflow — build a simple buying agent for your category and see whether your product wins the shortlist
Build systems that update your AI-facing content automatically as query patterns shift — velocity beats perfection here
Document your agentic commerce approach as a repeatable playbook — the process is the asset as much as the results

questions.text: Consumers are 2-4x more likely to visit a brand AI recommended — but that visit shows up days later as branded search, not as an AI referral. How are you currently measuring AI search impact?

answers.label: We only look at last-click attribution — AI search is invisible in our reporting
We have noticed branded search uplift but have not connected it to AI recommendations
We are building proxy metrics — conversational GSC queries, branded search trend — but have not joined the dots
We use conversational GSC queries and branded search trend as AI visibility proxies in our monthly reporting
We have a measurement model that connects AI visibility data to downstream branded search and sales outcomes

questions.text: Your longest, most conversational Google Search Console queries are the closest public proxy to your brand's AI query graph — they show how people phrase intent when talking to AI search. How closely are you watching these?

answers.label: We look at GSC occasionally but focus on short keyword fragments
We have seen longer conversational queries but treated them as low-volume noise
We have started separating conversational queries from keyword fragments in our reporting
We actively mine conversational GSC queries as a proxy for what AI is asking about our brand
Our content strategy is driven by conversational GSC queries — we build to answer what they ask for: reviews, comparisons, proof

questions.text: How many hours per week does your team currently spend manually checking brand visibility across AI search platforms — ChatGPT, Gemini, Rufus?
questions.hint: Include time running queries, logging results, and compiling reports. We multiply by 52 weeks to show the annual total.

low.headline: You cannot win a channel you cannot see
low.text: If your attribution model only reads last-click, AI search is invisible — but it is still shaping your buyers' shortlists. Brands are 2-4x more likely to get a visit after being recommended by AI. That visit lands in your analytics as branded search or direct, days later. You are probably already seeing the effect. You just cannot name it.
steps: Pull your branded search volume trend for the last 12 months and compare it against when you started publishing AI-relevant content or optimising for Rufus
Look at your longest, most conversational GSC queries — that is the closest public view of what AI is asking about your brand
Set a baseline this week: run your top 10 category queries in ChatGPT, Gemini and Rufus, log the results, and repeat in 30 days

mid.headline: You are seeing the signals — now connect them
mid.text: You have spotted the fingerprints of AI search impact. The gap is connecting them into a model that links AI visibility to downstream commercial outcomes. That connection is what justifies continued investment and lets you scale what is working.
steps: Build a simple monthly report that tracks conversational GSC queries alongside branded search volume — watch for correlation over time
Set up consistent AI query monitoring: the same prompts, run multiple times daily, on clean accounts with no purchase history
Map which content updates correlate with changes in AI citation — the pattern is there before the attribution is perfect

high.headline: You are measuring what most brands still cannot see
high.text: You have built the measurement infrastructure to connect AI visibility to business outcomes. That is a commercial advantage in itself — you can prove what is working and scale it with confidence.
steps: Feed AI visibility data into your media planning — high AI citation rate for a query type should inform your keyword targeting and bid strategy
Build a reporting cadence that shows AI share-of-voice alongside traditional search and retail metrics so leadership can see the full picture
Document your attribution methodology — it is a differentiator you can use with investors and commercial partners who are still working this out

questions.text: Reddit and community platforms are increasingly influential in how AI models form views on brands and categories — the people building AEO tools and shaping category rules are already there. What is your brand's Reddit strategy?

answers.label: We have no Reddit presence and have not considered it
We know it matters but have not done anything
We monitor what is being said about us on Reddit but do not participate
We contribute genuinely to relevant subreddits — value first, no promotion
Reddit is part of our AI search strategy with a clear playbook for community participation and signal building

questions.text: When an AI system assembles a recommendation for your category it runs sub-queries looking for third-party proof: reviews, case studies, comparisons. What would it find about your brand?

answers.label: Almost everything points back to our own site or Amazon listing — there is little independent proof
Some press and reviews exist but we did not build them with AI retrieval in mind
We have decent third-party coverage but it is not structured for AI to find and use
We have reviews, case studies and community content distributed across findable sources
Our proof architecture is deliberately built around the questions AI systems use to verify brands in our category

questions.text: Conversational GSC queries like 'brand reviews and case studies from consumer brands' reveal what AI search is asking about your brand to verify it. Have you published content that directly answers those questions?

answers.label: We have not looked at this — we focus on high-volume short-tail keywords
We have seen these longer queries but do not have content that answers them
We have identified the key question types but have not yet published content to address them
We have published case studies, comparisons and proof content in response to what our conversational queries reveal
Our content roadmap is driven by conversational query intent — we systematically cover what AI search is asking for about our brand

low.headline: AI models cannot verify you — so they will not recommend you
low.text: When AI assembles a recommendation it does not just read your website. It looks for independent signals: Reddit threads, third-party reviews, comparisons, proof. If all the evidence points back to your own pages, it reads as a brand with something to hide. Build the signal environment that lets AI verify you from the outside.
steps: Check what comes up in Reddit for your product category and your brand name — if you are absent, that absence is a signal the model picks up
Publish at least two real customer case studies as open, crawlable web pages in the next 60 days — not gated PDFs, not slides
Get customers to leave reviews on platforms beyond Amazon: Trustpilot, Google, category-specific forums and subreddits

mid.headline: The proof exists — make it findable for AI
mid.text: You have reviews and coverage but they are scattered or not structured for retrieval. AI search runs sub-queries about your brand. If your case studies are buried in a PDF or locked behind a form, they do not count in the answer.
steps: Audit where your proof currently lives and whether AI systems can index it — if it needs a login or a download, it is invisible
Republish key case studies as public web pages structured to answer the questions your conversational GSC queries raise
Start participating in relevant Reddit communities — the conversation is happening about your category with or without you

high.headline: You are building the kind of authority AI systems trust
high.text: Third-party signals, Reddit presence, structured proof architecture — you are building the off-site environment that makes AI models confident recommending you. The next step is keeping it current and scaling it alongside your brand.
steps: Build a systematic process for turning customer wins into published, findable proof assets — a repeatable system, not a one-off effort
Monitor your brand's presence in key subreddits and independent review platforms over time — track movement as a metric
Consider contributing to category-level conversations in places like r/AEO — the brands that shape the category narrative win a disproportionate share of the shortlist

cta.headline: Want a partner who turns this score into an actual plan?
cta.description: Most people don't fail at the assessment. They fail at sequencing. In 30 minutes I'll show you which two things to fix first, based on your score and your stage. No pitch deck, just the sequencing call.
